messages:
maria: quick q — compliance asking to pull SIEM exports for an upcoming audit. want to avoid giving auditors broad log access. what RBAC pattern do we want here?

jonathan: i'd prefer a dedicated role 'siem-audit-reader' bound to the SIEM export bucket only. No console access, just read/export for a specific date range. short TTL on the role.

akash: +1. also need a just-in-time approval step from secops before granting. auditors only get access windowed to the audit dates.

maria: ok. curious about KMS implications — the export bucket is encrypted with customer-managed key (alias/redwood-logs). if we grant the role, do we also give kms:Decrypt to auditors? worried about misuse.

jonathan: do NOT give auditors raw kms:Decrypt on the CMK. Instead create an encryption grant to the SIEM service principal that decrypts for export. For auditors, we grant access to the exported objects (S3/GCS) which are encrypted-at-rest but decrypted by the SIEM during export. auditors get object-level read from the storage, not direct CMK rights.

sophie: note from incident last month — we had a case where a key rotation removed service grant and exports started failing. export logs show: 
```
2026-02-12T03:14:22Z exportd ERROR: export failed: AccessDenied to key alias/redwood-logs for principal arn:siem:exporter
```
We should include key-rotation tests in the rollout checklist.

maria: good call. so RBAC: siem-audit-reader role + bucket/object read; KMS: leave CMK grants to SIEM service, not auditors. And TTL + JIT approval. anything else?

jonathan: also add 'no-keys-in-export' policy clause — exports must never include plaintext key material or secret fields. Implement export transform to redact sensitive PII before export.

akash: on the JIT flow: secops receives a Slack approval request and a short-lived IAM role is auto-created for 24h. After 24h role is revoked and the export objects are moved to a restricted archive with 90d retention.

maria: retention question — compliance asked for 7 years for some audit logs. our SIEM export retention is currently 90d. is that a blocker?

sophie: long-term retention for compliance needs offline/archive tier (cold storage) with stricter access controls and stronger audit trails. We can push exports to cold bucket with KMS key dedicated for long-term retention and more limited key admin RBAC.

jonathan: process note: when we rotate the archive CMK, create key grants for the SIEM service and schedule a dry-run to ensure exports still decrypt. Also update key policy to allow only 'siem-exporter' and 'seclog-archiver' principals, no human principals.

audit-bot: grant created: grant-id=gg-9a2f, principal=auditor-team, resource=gs://redwood-sei-exports/2026-02, expires=2026-02-20T23:59:59Z

maria: thanks — action items: 1) jonathan to draft RBAC role + example policy, 2) sophie to add key-rotation test to runbook, 3) akash to design JIT approval flow with 24h TTL, 4) maria to confirm retention requirements with legal. i'll open a GH issue and link the policy.

jonathan: will post a sample policy snippet here shortly.

akash: if anyone needs the incident log snippet from last month ping me, i'll attach it to the GH issue.

sophie: one more: add monitoring alert if export failures due to KMS errors exceed threshold (5 failures / 10m) so oncall gets paged before audits are impacted.

maria: perfect. thanks all :thumbsup:
